grammar: The grammars ISO/IEC 14882 defines for `std::basic_regex` ([re.grammar], [re.synopt]), production by production: ECMAScript's (ECMA-262, third edition, 15.10.1, the edition [intro.refs] cites, as [re.grammar] modifies it: ClassAtom and IdentityEscape modified, ClassAtomExClass, ClassAtomCollatingElement, ClassAtomEquivalence, ClassName and ClassNameCharacter added), POSIX's basic and extended regular expressions (XBD 9.5.2, with the bracket expression grammar both share, and 9.5.3), and what [re.synopt]'s awk, grep and egrep add to them (awk's escape sequences; grep's list of patterns). Each production or token is mapped to the kinds of Cpp RegExp it is read into (`kinds`, each `RegExp.<tag>`, a branch of `Expressions.Cpp.RegExp.Term`), with a `note` where it is read so in some of its alternatives alone, or is listed as not a kind (`not`), with its reason: a kind's property, a container of its terms, or a union of productions mapped each on its own. Every kind of the dialect is mapped from some production; its invalid syntax, `error` and `missing`, is the framework's, which no grammar has. Which grammar has each construct is checked by validation (`Expressions.Cpp.RegExp.FEATURES`).
checked: ISO/IEC 14882:2017, 2020 and 2024 (N4659, N4861 and N4950), whose [re.grammar] is the same in each; ECMA-262 3rd edition (1999); ISO/IEC/IEEE 9945:2009 (POSIX.1-2008), XBD 9.5, XCU awk and grep: 78 productions and tokens, written from the standards themselves, no parser being the reference for [re.grammar]
